question.problem:
There are three groups of fans in a certain town: those who prefer basketball, those who prefer baseball, and those who prefer football. A study has shown that, each year

- from the people that prefer basketball, $32%$ change to baseball and $28%$ change to football,

- from the people that prefer baseball, $45%$ change to football and $15%$ change to basketball,

- from the people that prefer football, $25%$ change to basketball and $65%$ change to baseball.

The stochastic matrix that describes this situation is given below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.15 & a \\ 0.32 & b & 0.65 \\ c & 0.45 & 0.1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
We are given the following situation for each year: - From the people who prefer basketball, $32%$ change to baseball and $28%$ change to football. This implies that $40%$ of them continue to prefer basketball. - From people who prefer baseball, $45%$ change to football and $15%$ change to basketball. This implies that $40%$ of them continue to prefer baseball. - From people who prefer football, $25%$ change to basketball and $65%$ change to baseball. This implies that $10%$ of them continue to prefer football. Writing this information in tabular form, we obtain the following:
From:
Basketball Baseball Football
To: Basketball $0.4$ $0.15$ $0.25$
Baseball $0.32$ $0.4$ $0.65$
Football $0.28$ $0.45$ $0.1$
We can write the corresponding stochastic matrix as follows: $$ P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.15 & 0.25 \\ 0.32 & 0.4 & 0.65 \\ 0.28 & 0.45 & 0.1\end{aligned}]. $$ Finally, we have $$ a+b+c=0.25+0.4+0.28=0.93. $$
